doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

chapter: Playing and listening in the moment
title: Using a music stand and 'map' of chord changes
summary: Friesen explains he needs a stand with tunes and chords since he has about 700 pieces on record.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know I noticed that in the videos, I’ve seen some videos of you and the drummer didn’t have a stand, and most of the time you did not have a music stand. So my assumption was that most of the music you were playing was yours, was your composition.

It is mine but I do need a stand. I’ve got to have a map in front of me because you know I think I have something like 700 pieces of music on record or CDs and I can’t remember everything, so I always have — and I’m writing music all the time. So no, I need a map up there for myself. Most of the things, the videos I see, I do see myself with a music stand.
Okay. When you say a “map,” is that different from when we think of a chart filled with notes and instructions. Is your map —
That — I call it a map, you know. It’s the chord changes, it’s the tune and the chords to it, yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
Yeah. I just called it a map. I didn’t want to confuse you. Sorry.
